title: How Do Pilots Find Their Way?

scenes.title: How Do Pilots Find Their Way?
scenes.text: The sky has no roads and no street signs. So how do pilots know which way to go? Let's find out!

scenes.title: The Old Ways
scenes.text: Long ago, pilots found their way with paper maps, a compass, and landmarks on the ground, like rivers, roads and railway lines. On cloudy days, that was really hard!

scenes.title: The Flight Plan
scenes.text: Before every flight, the pilots load a flight plan into the computer. It's a list of invisible points in the sky, called waypoints, joined up like a connect-the-dots puzzle.

scenes.title: Satellites
scenes.text: But how does the plane know where it is right now? Satellites! Dozens of GPS satellites circle high above the Earth. Each one sends out a radio signal saying where it is and what time it is. By listening to several of them at once, the plane works out exactly where it is.

scenes.title: Autopilot
scenes.text: Then the autopilot does the steering, flying smoothly from waypoint to waypoint, while the pilots keep a close watch the whole time.

scenes.title: Air Traffic Control
scenes.text: Down on the ground, air traffic controllers watch every plane on their radar screens. Like traffic lights for the sky, they keep planes safely apart, giving each one its own height and path.

scenes.title: Landing in Fog
scenes.text: Near the airport, the plane catches an invisible radio beam that leads straight down to the runway, like a guide rope. It works even in thick fog!

scenes.title: Remember!
scenes.text: Maps, flight plans, satellites, autopilot, air traffic control, and radio beams. That's how pilots find their way! See you on the next flight.
